metaTitle: Malaysia eSIM | Maxis & CelcomDigi Data Plans
metaDescription: Get online in Malaysia on Maxis and CelcomDigi with a data eSIM from $0.30/day. Install by scanning a QR code and keep your own number for calls and texts.
intro: An eSIMFlys eSIM connects your phone in Malaysia without visiting a store or removing the SIM you already use. You buy a plan, scan a QR code, and your data is ready to switch on as soon as you arrive. Because the eSIM handles data only, your current SIM stays in place, so your usual number keeps working for calls and texts.
countryContext: Malaysia is a Southeast Asian destination, whether you are passing through on a layover, travelling for business or staying longer for a holiday, and having data ready makes getting around and staying in touch simpler. eSIMFlys plans connect to Malaysian mobile networks, using Maxis 5G and CelcomDigi 5G. Buying before you travel means you arrive with a working data plan rather than looking for a SIM locally.
networkNotes: In Malaysia your eSIM connects through Maxis 5G and CelcomDigi 5G, choosing an available network automatically once you land. You do not pick the operator yourself or adjust any technical settings. As long as your handset is eSIM-capable and carrier-unlocked, it registers on a supported network when you turn the eSIM line on.
connectionDetails: Malaysia plans are fixed-data only, ranging across 1, 3, 5, 10, 20 and 50 GB, starting from $0.30/day. Validity is either 7 or 30 days, and every plan supports top-ups, so you can add more data without buying again. That covers maps, messaging, bookings, uploads and general browsing.
activationNotes: Install your eSIM over Wi-Fi before departure by scanning the QR code, but leave the line off until you reach Malaysia. Most plans start counting from the eSIM's first connection to a local network, not from when you paid. After you land, switch the eSIM line on and enable data roaming so it can register.
whyEsim: Rather than turning on roaming with your home carrier, an eSIM lets you buy a set amount of Malaysian data upfront, so the cost is clear before you go. And rather than finding and fitting a local SIM after arrival, you set it up in advance, skip swapping cards, and keep your home number active for calls and texts.

faqs.q: Which networks does the eSIM use, and is my phone supported?
faqs.a: In Malaysia the eSIM connects through Maxis 5G and CelcomDigi 5G, chosen automatically once you arrive. It works on eSIM-capable, carrier-unlocked phones, most iPhone XS and newer, Google Pixel 3 and newer, and Samsung Galaxy S20 and newer. Dial *#06# to check that your phone shows an EID.

faqs.q: When does my Malaysia plan start?
faqs.a: Most plans start when the eSIM first connects to a local network in Malaysia, not when you buy. That means you can install it on Wi-Fi before you fly. Your validity, either 7 or 30 days, then runs from that first connection.

faqs.q: Can I keep my usual phone number?
faqs.a: Yes. The eSIM is data-only, so your existing SIM stays in the phone and your usual number keeps handling calls and texts. To avoid charges on your home line, leave its data roaming off and rely on the eSIM for internet.

faqs.q: Which data size should I choose for Malaysia?
faqs.a: Pick based on your trip length and habits. A short visit using maps and messaging may only need 1, 3 or 5 GB, while longer stays or heavier browsing and uploads suit 10, 20 or 50 GB. Every Malaysia plan supports top-ups, so you can add more data if you run low.
